n.2: Omitting lessons damages long-term organisational learning.

14.q: A project manager is preparing a Gantt chart to outline when specific tasks will be carried out. What aspect of scheduling does this support?
14.w: Gantt charts are a common tool used in scheduling to define task order and timing.

n.1: Financial reporting is handled through the CBS and budget management.
n.2: While scheduling helps highlight risks, risk identification is a separate process.
n.3: Team assignments are managed through RAM and OBS, not the Gantt chart.
n.4: Procurement schedules are separate from the project task schedule.

14.q: You are overseeing a team delivering a new intranet for your company. Which action reflects project management activity?
o: Adjusting payroll settings for monthly cycles
Developing a risk log to manage delivery uncertainty
Running day-to-day maintenance on the old intranet
14.w: Managing delivery risks is part of the structured approach that defines project management.

n.0: Payroll tasks are routine operational work.
n.3: Timesheets support BAU administration, not project delivery.
n.2: Ongoing maintenance is not a project activity.
n.4: Procurement support is an administrative process, not project management.

14.q: A project team applies a cost of £2,000 per square metre to estimate the construction of a 500 m² office. Which estimating method are they using?
14.w: Parametric estimating applies known cost per unit to estimate total cost.

n.0: Analogous compares whole projects, not per-unit rates.
n.3: Analytical would involve calculating cost per task/item.
n.4: Expert judgement supports estimates but isn’t a method by itself.
n.1: Delphi requires multiple expert iterations.

14.q: What is a key difference between a project audit and a post-project review?
o: Audits focus on compliance and governance, reviews focus on performance and learning
Audits assess benefits, reviews assess schedules
Audits occur only in agile projects
Reviews are only for financial projects
14.w: Audits examine whether the project complied with organisational processes and standards, while reviews focus on results and lessons learned.

n.3: Audits apply across project types, not just agile.
n.4: Reviews are used in all project contexts, not just financial ones.
n.2: Benefit evaluation is part of benefit reviews, not audits.
n.1: There are clear differences between these processes.

14.q: Which stakeholder group is primarily responsible for ensuring that the project aligns with strategic objectives in the plan?
14.w: The sponsor ensures alignment of the project with business goals and justifies the plan.

n.3: Team members deliver tasks but don’t influence strategy.
n.0: The product owner focuses on product backlog and delivery, not business strategy.
n.2: Suppliers deliver inputs but don’t shape objectives.
n.1: Scrum masters facilitate delivery but don’t set strategic aims.

14.q: What is one of the disadvantages of using physical noticeboards for communication?
o: They rely on stakeholders physically being present to see updates
They are interactive and easy to update remotely
They offer automatic backup of content
14.w: Physical noticeboards are static and only useful to those who can access them in person.

n.2: They are not interactive or remote-friendly.
n.0: There is no chat feature.
n.3: Content must be updated manually.
n.4: Video is not supported.

14.q: A sponsor has just signed off the project business case and committed the funding. What should be their next priority?
o: Planning the benefit review meetings alone
Ensuring the project aligns to strategic objectives and governance
14.w: A key sponsor responsibility is to ensure the project stays strategically aligned and adheres to governance standards.

n.3: Schedule development is led by the project manager.
n.4: This level of detail is not within the sponsor’s remit.
n.0: Procurement is typically managed by the PM or support functions.
n.1: Sponsors may attend benefit reviews, but planning them is a PMO or PM task.

14.q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between a PBS and a WBS?
o: The PBS outlines people, while the WBS outlines cost
The PBS sets the project budget, and the WBS sets the time limits
The PBS defines risks, and the WBS defines risk responses
The PBS is optional, while the WBS is legally required
The PBS outlines deliverables, and the WBS outlines the work required to create them
14.w: The PBS defines the product's components, while the WBS details the work needed to create those components.

n.0: Neither PBS nor WBS define people; that's the OBS.
n.2: PBS and WBS are not used for risk management.
n.3: There is no legal requirement prioritising WBS over PBS.
n.1: Cost and time are managed by CBS and schedule management respectively.

14.q: A supplier requests a change to a component due to a manufacturing constraint. The project manager initiates a change request. What process will determine whether this change is accepted?
14.w: Change control is the process used to formally evaluate and decide on requested changes to scope or deliverables.

n.0: Stakeholder engagement is about communication and influence, not formal approvals.
n.2: Risk escalation deals with unresolved threats, not scope changes.
n.1: Scheduling is unrelated to whether the change is accepted.
n.4: Scope definition occurs early — this is about change to existing scope.

14.q: A project sponsor wants flexibility to refine product requirements as user needs emerge. Which life cycle approach is better suited to this and why?
o: Iterative, because it removes the need for planning
Linear, because it handles uncertainty best
Linear, because it freezes scope from the start
Linear, because it speeds up delivery by avoiding change
Iterative, because it supports evolving scope through continuous feedback
14.w: Iterative life cycles like Agile accommodate changing requirements by design, supporting evolving scope.

n.2: Linear approaches restrict changes once scope is set.
n.3: Linear avoids change but may not meet evolving needs.
n.0: Iterative still involves detailed planning at each cycle.
n.1: Iterative projects manage uncertainty, but not necessarily better than linear in all cases.
